Status: still counting. CA SOS Unprocessed Ballots Report (Nov 6) lists ~4,816,722 ballots still unprocessed; counting them would put CA near 59.0%, above 2022's 50.8%. CA SOS total-registration basis is consistent across all years, and CA has never finished a midterm below 50.8% on it — 38.3% is a floor, not a result (notes §3.1).

Largest genuine-looking increase in the set (notes §3.2). Ballots rose 22.1% on essentially flat rolls (+0.8%); same SOS basis all years (rolls include Election Day registrations; no active/inactive split). A contested 2026 governor's race is a plausible behavioural driver but no mechanical, basis, or counting cause is documented in the files — verify against the final canvass.

The SOS 'registered at 7 a.m.' pre-registered count is constructed identically in 2018, 2022 and 2026, yet grew +10.2% vs 2022 (and +18.5% vs 2018) — far faster than Minnesota's adult population (2020 VAP 4,389,033). No cause is documented in the compiled files; the jump is in pre-registrations recorded before Election Day, not in the (separately explained) denominator construction.

Mirrors the ballots surge on a fixed 2020 VAP denominator (1,376,400): Idaho cast ballots equal to 53.2% of its entire 2020 adult population, vs 43.6% in 2022 — the same unexplained increase as the ballots and turnout rows.

Documented mechanical cause: Wyoming's post-election purges of non-voters shrink the rolls (rolls fell ~86,000 after 2022 per notes §3.7); 2026 rolls (281,219) sit -6.9% below 2022 while most states' rolls grew. The small, aggressively maintained denominator is also what inflates WY's turnout rates (notes §5).
463,912 ballots vs 597,149 in 2018 (-22.3%) and 493,910 in 2022 (-6.1%) on near-identical rolls; steepest real midterm-on-midterm ballots decline in the set after still-counting Alaska (notes §3.4).

Rolls grew +5.0% vs 2022 (1,210,385 vs 1,153,232, total basis both years) in the same cycle that ballots fell -6.1% — rolls and participation moving in opposite directions; no list-maintenance or basis explanation is documented in the files.

No 2022 comparison exists: the 2022 EAVS Wisconsin brief was not retrievable (documented gap, notes §4), so this row ranks on its 2018 deviation. The 2026 numerator is governor-race votes — a top-race proxy that understates total ballots cast — whereas 2018 is EAVS F1a total turnout; rolls also grew +192,842 on essentially flat ballots (-1.0%), so the rate fell through the denominator and the proxy, not through voting (notes §3.5).

Same total-registration basis in all years (notes §3.4: 'genuine decline'). Ballots fell while rolls grew; West Virginia elects its governor in presidential years, so 2026 had no governor's race — a plausible salience driver, but behavioural, not mechanical; nothing in the files accounts for the drop.

Same ballots increase as the ballots row on a fixed 2020 VAP denominator (7,914,602): Michigan cast ballots equal to 61.2% of its 2020 adult population, second-highest in the nation, with no published registration total to pair it with.

Ballots exceed both prior midterms (+2.3% vs 2022; +10.6% vs 2018) on SOS total-ballots-cast figures in all years (2018 SOS 580,214 used, not the EAVS 581,551). No counting, basis, or mechanical cause is documented in the files; the 2026 figure was reported as 'more than 641,625', so it is a floor.

2026 value is a matched set of 35 states reporting both figures, on mixed registration bases (active-only in FL/OR/UT/NV, total elsewhere), preliminary, with top-race proxy ballots in 11 states; the 2022 value is the final EAVS national total-basis rate. Notes §1: 'not yet a national turnout rate.' No 2018 rate exists (EAC published only 'more than 211 million' registered).

The comparison spans a basis switch: 2018 is EAVS total registered, 2022 is EAVS active registered (A1b), and purge-shrunk denominators inflate the rate in all years; notes §3.7 call cross-year WY comparisons the widest error bars in the set.

Documented mechanical cause: the denominator is voters registered at 7 a.m. on Election Day (pre-registered only) while the numerator includes Election Day registrants, inflating the rate in every year on an identical construction (78.8 / 70.9 / 88.8 / 72.6). Within that constant construction 2026 sits between its two midterm marks — no behavioural anomaly (notes §3.6, §5). The 2026 numerator is additionally an SOS estimate.
